newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea's crippled economy shrinks again - Seoul.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea's crippled economy shrinks again - Seoul.

text.p: Crippled by shortages of energy and raw materials, North Korea's economy shrank for the seventh year in a row in 1996, South Korea's central bank said on Wednesday.
Gross domestic product dropped by a real 3.7 percent following a 4.6 percent decline in 1995, the Bank of Korea said in a report.
Since the secretive Stalinist nation does not release economic statistics, the central bank's data is largely based on educated guess-work.

Farm, forestry and fishery output rose by 1.0 percent in 1996 after falling 10.5 percent the previous year, the report said. Manufacturing and construction output was down by 8.9 percent and 11.8 percent respectively.

"Production in manufacturing and most other industrial sectors fell sharply due to the short supply of energy and raw materials and troubles in transportation systems resulting from a delayed recovery from floods," the report said.
Per-capita Gross National Product in the famine-stricken nation dropped to $910 in 1996 from $957 in 1995. South Korea's per-capital GNP last year hit $10,548.
